blocks.content: The Indian National Movement was the struggle of the Indian people to achieve independence from British colonial rule. It developed gradually during the 19th and 20th centuries and involved political movements, mass protests, and revolutionary activities.
1. Background of Indian National Movement

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The freedom struggle progressed through three main eras: Moderate Phase (1885–1905), Extremist Phase (1905–1919), and the Gandhian Phase.
Important early resistance movements included the Swadeshi Movement and Home Rule Movement (1916).
Major nationwide mass mobilizations under Mahatma Gandhi were the Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–1922) and Civil Disobedience Movement (1930–1934).
The Quit India Movement was launched in 1942, serving as the final major mass protest leading to the Independence of India.

blocks.content: • British economic exploitation caused poverty and dissatisfaction among Indians.
• Educated Indians started demanding political rights and reforms.
• The spread of modern education and press created political awareness.
• Social and religious reform movements also contributed to national consciousness.
2. Formation of Indian National Congress (INC)
The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by A.O. Hume. The first session of the Congress was held in Bombay in 1885.
3. Moderate Phase (1885–1905)
• Moderates believed in constitutional methods.
• They used petitions, meetings and discussions to present demands.
• Important leaders: Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Surendranath Banerjee.
• They demanded greater representation for Indians in government.
4. Extremist Phase (1905–1919)
• Extremists believed in more aggressive methods.
• They promoted Swadeshi and Boycott movements.
• Important leaders: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai.
• The partition of Bengal in 1905 intensified the nationalist movement.
5. Swadeshi Movement
• Started after the partition of Bengal in 1905.
• People boycotted British goods.
• Encouraged the use of Indian-made goods.
• Promoted national education and indigenous industries.
6. Home Rule Movement (1916)
• Launched by Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant.
• Demanded self-government for India.
• It helped to spread political awareness among the masses.
7. Gandhian Phase of the National Movement
• Mahatma Gandhi introduced the method of Satyagraha.
• He mobilized masses including peasants and workers.
• Major movements included Non-Cooperation Movement, Civil Disobedience Movement, and Quit India Movement.
8. Non-Cooperation Movement (1920–1922)
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi.
• People boycotted British goods, schools, courts and titles.
• The movement was withdrawn after the Chauri Chaura incident.
9. Civil Disobedience Movement (1930–1934)
• Began with the famous Dandi March in 1930.
• Gandhi broke the salt law to protest British policies.
• It became a nationwide movement.
10. Quit India Movement (1942)
• Launched on 8 August 1942.
• Gandhi gave the slogan 'Do or Die'.
• It demanded immediate independence for India.
11. Independence of India

items: Chronological sequence questions frequently test the years: Moderate Phase (1885–1905), Extremist Phase (1905–1919), Home Rule Movement (1916), Non-Cooperation (1920–1922), Civil Disobedience (1930–1934), and Quit India Movement (1942).
Pay attention to the exact duration of key mass movements for direct MCQs in Indian competitive exams.

blocks.content: • India gained independence on 15 August 1947.
• The country was partitioned into India and Pakistan.
• Jawaharlal Nehru became the first Prime Minister of independent India.
SSC Exam Important Facts
• Indian National Congress was founded in 1885.
• A.O. Hume played a key role in its formation.
• Partition of Bengal took place in 1905.
• Quit India Movement started in 1942.
• India became independent on 15 August 1947.
